deals.handout: South bids 2 NT to show game forcing hand with 4 hearts. North shows a minimum with a 4♥ bid, ending the auction.

problems.explanation: You have four hearts and 13 HCP: an opening hand with a fit. Bid 2NT, Jacoby: four or more trumps and game values. Partner will describe their hand.

whyNot.3H: 3♥ is a limit raise, about 10–12. You have an opening hand.
whyNot.4H: A jump to 4♥ is weak and distributional. You have 13 HCP and want to find out about slam.

problems.explanation: Partner's 2NT is Jacoby: four or more hearts and game values. You have no singleton or void and a minimum, 13, so jump to 4♥.

whyNot.3H: 3♥ shows 18 or more. You have a minimum.
whyNot.3C: A new suit at the three level shows a singleton or void. You have none.

deals.handout: West has a solid game force with 4 spades and bids 2 NT. East shows singleton diamond with 3♦. West has worst possible diamond holding and signs off in 4♠.

problems.explanation: You have four spades and 16 HCP. Bid 2NT, Jacoby: four or more trumps and game values, and partner describes their hand.

whyNot.3S: 3♠ is a limit raise, about 10–12. You have 16.
whyNot.4S: A jump to 4♠ is weak and distributional. You have 16 and slam is possible.

problems.explanation: Partner's 2NT is Jacoby. You have a singleton diamond, so bid 3♦ to show it. Partner can judge how well the hands fit.

whyNot.4S: 4♠ shows a minimum with no singleton or void. Show your singleton.
whyNot.3S: 3♠ shows 18 or more and no singleton. You have a singleton diamond.
whyNot.3N: 3NT shows 15–17 and no singleton. You have a singleton diamond.

problems.explanation: Partner has a singleton diamond, and your KQJ there are wasted: partner will ruff the suit anyway. That's the worst holding opposite a singleton, so sign off in 4♠.

whyNot.4N: Your diamond honours are wasted opposite the singleton. Slam is unlikely.
whyNot.3S: Your diamond honours are wasted. Sign off in game.

deals.handout: North has an opening hand with 4 spades and bids 2 NT. South shows 15-17 without shortness by bidding 3 NT. North should signoff in 4♠ over that.

problems.explanation: You have four spades and 13 HCP. Bid 2NT, Jacoby: four or more trumps and game values.

whyNot.3S: 3♠ is a limit raise, about 10–12. You have an opening hand.
whyNot.4S: A jump to 4♠ is weak and distributional.

problems.explanation: Partner's 2NT is Jacoby. You have no singleton or void, and 15 HCP, so bid 3NT: 15–17 without shortness. It doesn't mean you want to play notrump.

whyNot.3C: A new suit at the three level shows a singleton or void. You have none.

problems.explanation: Partner has 15–17 and no shortness. You have 13 and a balanced hand, without the extras for slam. Sign off in 4♠.

whyNot.4N: You have a minimum opening hand with no shortness, and partner hasn't shown more than 17. Sign off.
whyNot.P: 3NT shows strength, not a wish to play there. You have a spade fit.

deals.handout: East has an opening hand with 4 hearts and bids 2 NT. West shows a good 5 card diamond suit with 4♦. Note, the East hand bids slam over 4♦ while he would sign off in 4H over a 3♣ bid showing short clubs.

problems.explanation: You have four hearts and 14 HCP. Bid 2NT, Jacoby: four or more trumps and game values.

whyNot.3H: 3♥ is a limit raise, about 10–12. You have an opening hand.
whyNot.4H: A jump to 4♥ is weak and distributional.

acceptable.3C: Showing the singleton club is also descriptive. The handout prefers 4♦ for the strong second suit, which East likes more.

problems.explanation: Partner's 2NT is Jacoby. You have a strong second suit, five diamonds with two of the top three honours, so jump to 4♦ to show it.

whyNot.4H: 4♥ shows a minimum with no shortness or second suit. Your diamonds are worth showing.

problems.explanation: Partner has a good five-card diamond suit, and your KJ of diamonds fills it in. With 14 HCP, four hearts and that fit, slam is likely. Bid 4NT, RKCB, to check key cards.

whyNot.4H: Your diamond honours fit partner's second suit perfectly. Look for slam.

problems.explanation: Partner's 4NT is RKCB for hearts. You have two key cards (the ♥A and ♦A) and the ♥Q, so bid 5♠: two key cards with the queen.

whyNot.5H: 5♥ shows two key cards without the queen of trumps. You have the ♥Q.
whyNot.5C: 5♣ shows one or four key cards. You have two.

problems.explanation: Partner has two key cards and the ♥Q. With your ♠A and ♥K that's four of the five: only the ♣A is missing. Bid 6♥.

whyNot.7H: You're missing a key card, the ♣A.
whyNot.5N: 5NT asks about kings for a grand slam, which needs all five key cards. You're missing one.

deals.handout: North shows shortness in diamonds with the 3♦ bid. South's hand is not bad opposite
reviewNotes: The handout's explanation is cut off. The RKCB answers follow the RKCB lesson (1430, and the lowest king for 5NT). South's 3♠ and North's 4NT and 5NT aren't problems because the text doesn't cover them.

problems.explanation: You have four spades and 13 HCP. Bid 2NT, Jacoby: four or more trumps and game values.

whyNot.3S: 3♠ is a limit raise, about 10–12. You have an opening hand.
whyNot.4S: A jump to 4♠ is weak and distributional.

problems.explanation: Partner's 2NT is Jacoby. You have a singleton diamond, so show it with 3♦, even with 18 HCP. Partner can judge how well the hands fit.

whyNot.3S: 3♠ shows 18 or more with no singleton or void. Show your singleton first.
whyNot.4S: 4♠ shows a minimum with no shortness.
whyNot.4H: Jumping in a new suit shows a strong five-card suit. Your hearts are four long.

problems.explanation: Partner's 4NT is RKCB for spades. You have three key cards: the ♠K, ♦A and ♣A. Bid 5♦: zero or three.

whyNot.5C: 5♣ shows one or four key cards. You have three.
whyNot.5H: 5♥ shows two key cards. You have three: the ♠K counts.

problems.explanation: Partner's 5NT asks for your lowest king outside trumps. The ♠K doesn't count, and you have no other king, so bid 6♠.

whyNot.6D: You have no ♦K. With no king outside trumps, bid six of the trump suit.
whyNot.7S: Partner is asking about kings, not telling you to bid seven.

deals.handout: East shows short clubs with a 3♣ bid. West stalls with 3♠. East shows a minimum with 4♠. West is close to bidding over this but should give up.
reviewNotes: The Jacoby 2NT text doesn't cover responder's rebids, like West's 3♠ "stall". That problem and its explanation follow the handout's comments.

problems.explanation: You have four spades and 16 HCP. Bid 2NT, Jacoby: four or more trumps and game values.

whyNot.3S: 3♠ is a limit raise, about 10–12. You have 16.
whyNot.4S: A jump to 4♠ is weak and distributional.

problems.explanation: Partner's 2NT is Jacoby. You have a singleton club, so bid 3♣ to show it.

whyNot.4S: 4♠ shows a minimum with no singleton. Show your singleton.

problems.explanation: Partner has a singleton club, and your ♣AK are partly wasted there. Slam is less likely, but with 16 you're not ready to give up. Bid 3♠, the cheapest way to agree spades and wait to hear more.

whyNot.4S: With 16 you can afford to keep the bidding low and hear more from partner first.
whyNot.4N: Your club honours are partly wasted opposite the singleton. Find out more before asking for key cards.

problems.explanation: Partner's 3♠ waits for more information. You have a minimum, 12, so bid 4♠.

whyNot.4N: You have a minimum and have already shown your singleton. Leave slam to partner.

problems.explanation: Partner has shown a minimum. Your ♣AK are partly wasted opposite the singleton club, so slam is unlikely. You're close, but pass.

whyNot.4N: Partner has a minimum and your clubs are wasted. Give up on slam.
